qc.label_under_test: Dense / gate-leak background unit: the - pole is a weak leak (max 1.52, 11% of tokens above 0.1 of max, 99.6% '-g +u leak') that hums at about 0.1-0.3 of max on most prose. Its feeders ('late' in any sense, lateness words, 'belated', 'little', ambient-it predicates) add only a small bump, so 'too late' / 'too little, too late' does not separate from matched text without lateness; the slightly stronger pockets are clinical-psychology / talking-therapy text (the + pole's topic leaking through) and the headline 'Too Little too Late?'.

neighbours.label: Weak leak pole whose real driver is therapy / treatment text, strongest for mental-health treatment (talking therapy, counselling, psychotherapy, ECT, therapy groups at a clinic; speech therapy also counts). Lateness feeders ('late', 'too little, too late') add only a smaller second pocket in the fixed idiom; plain lateness does not fire it.
fire: Counselling is a talking therapy offered free by many GP surgeries.
She started weekly psychotherapy sessions to work through her grief.
Cognitive behavioural therapy teaches patients to challenge anxious thoughts.
Electroconvulsive therapy is sometimes used when antidepressants fail.
The clinic runs a group therapy session for veterans every Thursday.
A speech therapist helped the boy pronounce his first words clearly.
Family therapy can help parents and teenagers communicate better.
Psychoanalysis grew out of Freud's early work with hysterical patients.
quiet: Her doctor measured her blood pressure and weight at the checkup.
She started weekly piano lessons to fill her quiet evenings.
The hospital car park was full by nine o'clock on Monday.
The pharmacy closes early on Sundays and public holidays.
The library runs a book club for retirees every Thursday.
